newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spot mixed.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spot mixed.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed up on Monday due to rises in the A share markets and a new issue on the Shenzhen stock exchange, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active three-day contract rose to 16.58 from 4.70 percent last Friday.
Total turnover rose to 11.95 million lots from 6.59 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
The strong rises in both Shanghai and Shenzhen A shares and a new issue today in Shenzhen helped to push the early-maturing contracts up sharply, traders said.
"There will be several new issues in both Shanghai and Shenzhen this week, which is likely to support the three-day and seven-day contracts to higher levels in the next few days," one trader said.
Rumours that the central bank would not cut bank interest rates before the Chinese lunar new year also helped today's rise on the repo market, traders added.
But contracts on Shanghai's T-bill spot market ended mixed on the same rumours, pushing down the most active three-year note which matures in 1999, traders said.
The three-year note fell to 103.30 yuan from 103.65 yuan last Friday. Turnover of the bond was 0.97 billion yuan.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market fell to 2.14 million lots from 3.42 million.
"The rumours hit the confidence of some long-term investors," one trader said.
But traders said the upward trend of the spots since last week would not change in the short-term as a result of expectations that new issues this year will be priced low.
"The comparatively high coupon of the three-year bond will continue to attract long-term buyers in the next few days," said one local trader.
